answer: Each AI agent must register a remote attestation from a secure enclave that binds its identity to the frequency skew of a quartz oscillator PUF; the registry stores these fingerprints in a Merkle summit and rejects a duplicate leaf, so one physical chip can mint only one identity. A saffron tamper coating zeroizes the PUF if opened, and an attacker must buy a separate attestation chip per fake agent, roughly sixty dollars plus three watts of power for hourly renewals.
